articles.title: Home Assistant turns an error log into a prepared bug report
articles.dek: A link chooses the appropriate issue tracker and fills in the error and software version.
body: People reporting a Home Assistant problem gain a direct route from an error’s log details to a prepared bug report. The link opens the appropriate tracker for Core or the interface and fills in the selected log, the Core version and integration details where available.

Custom integrations use their own supplied issue tracker. Aidan Timson also adds links to reporting guidance, helping people find the right destination without reconstructing the diagnostic details by hand.

articles.title: Home Assistant gives each home its own phone-sensor choices
articles.dek: The Apple app can share different readings with different servers instead of sending every home the same set.
body: Home Assistant’s Apple app lets people choose a separate set of phone sensors for each connected home. Enabling a sensor was previously a device-wide choice, so every server receiving sensors got the same selection.

The Sensors settings screen opens each home’s own choices. Existing servers inherit the selection they already shared, while a newly added server starts with no sensors enabled. The update interval and device permissions remain shared.

This extends the setup consent reported on September 21: people can decide which individual readings to share with each home, beyond the earlier choice of whether that home receives sensor data at all.

articles.title: Home Assistant tackles iOS 27 dashboard lag with a security tradeoff
articles.dek: Plain-HTTP connections bypass an extra WebKit security mode by default, with a setting to restore it.
body: Home Assistant’s Apple app changes a browser security setting to tackle severe dashboard lag on iOS 27. Bruno Pantaleão Gonçalves reports that WebKit puts unencrypted HTTP pages in an enhanced-security process even on a private home network, while the same dashboard over HTTPS avoids that behavior.

When a configured server uses plain HTTP, the app disables the preference that selects that extra security mode. A General setting restores Apple’s default for people who prefer to keep the additional protection.

Gonçalves verified the process selection in a basic WebKit browser view, but a check against Home Assistant on a real device remains outstanding. The preference is undocumented and could change in a later Apple update.

articles.title: Music Assistant restores albums that YouTube Music leaves unplayable
articles.dek: Albums could fail during playback and synchronization, or appear with no playable tracks.
body: Music Assistant repairs a YouTube Music album lookup that could fail whenever someone tried to play or synchronize an affected album. It also restores track information missing from anonymous album requests, which could leave an album with no playable tracks.
Ralf Heiringhoff uses the listener’s existing authentication for the lookup and handles a missing playlist reference. This is his first contribution to the Music Assistant server, reviewed by OzGav.

pullRequests.title: Fix YTMusic album resolution crash on null audioPlaylistId

articles.title: Apple Watch reaches Home Assistant through the iPhone’s home connection
articles.dek: Relaying requests fixes local controls on networks that cannot route their public address back into the home.
body: Home Assistant restores Apple Watch controls on home networks where the public server address cannot be reached from inside. The watch previously always chose the remote address, even when its traffic passed through an iPhone connected to the home Wi-Fi.

When the paired iPhone is immediately reachable, it performs the request using its own choice of local or remote connection. The watch keeps its credentials and handles the result. If the relay is unavailable before a request reaches the network, the watch uses its own connection.

articles.title: Music Assistant levels Tidal tracks without a preliminary scan
articles.dek: Loudness information supplied by Tidal lets volume normalization work from the start.
body: Music Assistant uses loudness information supplied by Tidal to even out differences in track volume without first scanning the audio. Tidal listeners benefit from the service’s existing measurements instead of waiting for Music Assistant to measure each track itself.
Dorian Stoll makes his first contribution to the Music Assistant server with the work. It builds on the existing support for loudness data supplied by other music sources.

pullRequests.title: Use the loudness provided by Tidal

articles.title: Home Assistant includes device parts when targeting a parent’s label
articles.dek: An action aimed at a labeled power strip also reaches its child outlets.
body: Home Assistant includes a device’s child parts when an action targets a label attached to the parent. For example, a label on a power strip also selects its child outlets, matching what happens when the parent device is targeted directly.
Artur Pragacz changes action targeting rather than copying labels onto the children. A label attached only to one child continues to target that child alone.

pullRequests.title: Include child devices when targeting a labelled parent device

articles.title: ESPHome keeps renamed devices reachable for firmware updates
articles.dek: Device Builder remembers the name still running on a device when its configuration changes first.
body: Renaming an ESPHome device without immediately installing new firmware could leave every later upload looking for a network name the device did not yet use. Device Builder remembers the old name so an installation can still reach it, instead of requiring the maker to rename the configuration back.

J. Nick Koston covers rename commands and direct edits to the device name. The remembered name is a fallback when the new one cannot be found and is cleared after a successful installation. Devices using only the web server still need to be discovered under their new name before an offline status can recover.

pullRequests.title: Remember the hostname a flash-free rename leaves on the device

articles.title: Assist expands Basque commands for floors, scripts and scenes
articles.dek: More ways to switch devices on and off join clearer spoken responses.
body: Basque speakers gain Assist commands for switching devices by floor, starting named scripts and scenes, and addressing cover types across a room or floor. The language rules fill missing combinations in the existing on and off commands rather than introducing Basque voice control for the first time.
Urtzi Odriozola also expands polite phrasing and corrects requests referring to “here.” Replies for named covers, locks and valves include the device’s name.

pullRequests.title: [eu] Complete HassTurnOn/TurnOff coverage and fix rules, errors and responses

articles.title: Music Assistant stops announcing populated settings lists as empty
articles.dek: Screen readers can identify the rows in music-source settings, setup steps and other shared lists.
body: Music Assistant gives screen readers the missing structure inside several settings and setup lists. Lists of music sources, background tasks, setup steps and user roles could be announced as empty because their rows did not identify themselves as list items.
Marcel van der Veldt fixes the shared row component so assistive technology can announce each list’s count and structure. The visual appearance stays the same.

pullRequests.title: Announce list rows to screen readers in settings lists

articles.title: Home Assistant keeps separate SleepIQ beds that share a sleeper
articles.dek: A duplicate filter no longer discards a real bed because one person appears in both profiles.
body: Home Assistant keeps separate SleepIQ beds on accounts where a person is associated with both. The previous duplicate filter treated any overlapping sleeper profile as evidence of duplication, silently removing a real second bed at each setup.

The filter compares the complete sleeper sets and uses foundation-feature information to distinguish controller duplicates. The correction preserves the original protection against duplicate “Firmness Control” devices.

pullRequests.title: Fix SleepIQ bed dedup removing real beds that share a sleeper

articles.title: Home Assistant explains how to connect distant serial devices
articles.dek: New guidance covers local USB adapters, ESPHome proxies and stable port selection.
body: Home Assistant’s serial guide walks through connecting equipment such as an AV receiver or energy meter either by a nearby USB adapter or through an ESPHome device beside the equipment. It explains how to check the available ports and choose the connection in the equipment’s integration.

The guide recommends stable serial identifiers instead of numbered USB paths that can change. A companion ESPHome overview explains Bluetooth, infrared, radio and serial proxies, and makes clear that serial proxies require a configuration you write and install yourself.
